rules.title: Coroutines live in a scope
rules.what: Launch coroutines from a scope with a lifetime (viewModelScope, lifecycleScope, a CoroutineScope you cancel), never GlobalScope.
rules.why: A GlobalScope coroutine outlives the screen or request that started it: on a phone, work and radio use continue for a screen already closed.
rules.how: viewModelScope.launch { ... }; structured concurrency with coroutineScope { }; cancel the custom scope on teardown.

patterns.note: GlobalScope coroutine: no lifetime, no cancellation.

verify.how: A test cancels the scope and asserts no child coroutine is still active.

rules.title: No blocking inside coroutines
rules.what: Use delay() in suspending code and withContext(Dispatchers.IO) for blocking work; keep runBlocking for main() and tests.
rules.why: runBlocking or Thread.sleep pins a dispatcher thread; a handful are enough to starve the pool and keep cores busy waiting.
rules.how: Replace Thread.sleep with delay; wrap blocking I/O in withContext(Dispatchers.IO).

patterns.note: Blocking call; fine in main() and tests only.

verify.how: No runBlocking or Thread.sleep outside main() and tests.

rules.title: Bounded channels
rules.what: Size channels to what the consumer absorbs and choose the overflow policy deliberately; no Channel.UNLIMITED.
rules.why: An unlimited channel removes back-pressure: the queue grows to whatever memory allows, and work is done twice, to enqueue then discard.
rules.how: Channel(capacity = 64, onBufferOverflow = BufferOverflow.SUSPEND); buffer() with a size on flows.

verify.how: Every channel declares a capacity and overflow policy.

rules.title: Sequences for long chains, sets for lookups
rules.what: On large collections, chain transformations through asSequence() and look up in a Set or Map instead of contains() on a List inside a loop.
rules.why: Each map/filter on a List allocates a full copy; contains on a List inside a loop turns the work quadratic.
rules.how: list.asSequence().filter{}.map{}.toList(); val ids = items.mapTo(HashSet()) { it.id } before the loop.

patterns.note: Three chained list transformations; candidate for asSequence() on large inputs.

verify.how: Benchmark or allocation profile on representative volume when the change is performance-motivated.

limits: On small collections a plain List chain is clearer and cheaper; a hit is a question about volume, not a defect.
